GainsBlock.rationale: `public override bool GainsBlock => true` (Taunt.cs:16) == the class attribute -- notable because Taunt is a SKILL that targets an enemy AND gains block, so neither the type nor the target type implies the flag.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Taunt.cs:26-29) == cost 1 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / ANY_ENEMY -- another enemy-targeting Skill, like card/dark_shackles and card/dominate.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new BlockVar(7m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new PowerVar<VulnerablePower>(1m)` (Taunt.cs:18-22) == both numbers, both declared. Move without Unpowered -> POWERED block, so NOT in gap G1's blast radius.

OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The card's own `if not target.is_gone:` is DELETED and PowerCmd.apply now carries the WHOLE of `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-322): `cmds.can_receive_powers` is `not target.is_removed_from_combat and hooks.should_allow_hitting(target)`, and `Creature.is_removed_from_combat` (creatures.py) is `is_gone and not retained_after_death` -- the sim's expression of `CombatState == null`, since it never drops a corpse from `enemies` (conformance addresses enemies by index). The two edits are a MATCHED PAIR: round 6 had wired only the ShouldAllowHitting half here, so deleting the card guard on its own would have powered the ordinary corpse that CreatureCmd.cs:523-531 removes. Pinned by test/test_can_receive_powers.py -- ordinary corpse refused, removal-vetoed corpse powered, mid-revival corpse still refused. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE: the observable the entry proposed -- a Vicious draw off a retained corpse -- is not reachable in the sim's SHIPPED content, and the enumeration is the finding. Every sim producer of a retained corpse also makes it unhittable for as long as it lasts (IllusionPower.cs:95-105, AdaptablePower.cs:68-78 and ReattachPower.cs:74-86 each pair the removal veto with ShouldAllowHitting), the sole exception being a Decimillipede segment killed with every other segment already down -- and that ends the combat, so PowerCmd.Apply's own IsEnding guard (PowerCmd.cs:69-72) swallows it first. The game's third case, PainfulStabsPower.cs:29-32 on Test Subject phase 2, retains WITHOUT vetoing hits and the sim's PainfulStabsPower omits that override; recorded here rather than fixed, because it is not this entry's line. The code is now the source's shape either way.  The text it replaced read: C# applies the debuff unconditionally and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose doc comment states that DEAD creatures can still receive powers -- it refuses only for a REMOVED corpse. The two agree for an ordinary kill (`CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `Kill` before returning, CreatureCmd.cs:409, removal at 523-525) and diverge for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; the sim's `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104), because `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Observable through ViciousPower, which draws on any Vulnerable its owner applies with no liveness test on the target (ViciousPower.cs:19-26). Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3); LIVE. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/card_probes.py dead-target-guards` lists 41 sim card classes that test liveness. Block 7 FIRST then Vulnerable 1 -- amounts and order faithful (Taunt.cs:35-36). Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (34) and the Vulnerable hover tip (24).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Block.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` + `DynamicVars.Vulnerable.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (Taunt.cs:41-42) == `_block += 1` (7 -> 8) and `_vulnerable += 1` (1 -> 2). Both upgraded numbers checked, and the +1 block is unusually small -- the common value is +3 -- so it is easy to transcribe wrongly.
